gary_2026_09_10_an_unmuted_debate_ai_edu.title: An UNMUTED Debate - AI & Education
gary_2026_09_10_an_unmuted_debate_ai_edu.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_10_an_unmuted_debate_ai_edu.summary: Gary's Guide: DOORS OPEN AT 6:30, SHOW STARTS AT 7 Majoring in AI, Minoring in Education? For decades, higher ed has sold two things at once & dared you not to notice: an education & a credential. The lecture & the diploma. The learning & the line on your resume. You couldn't buy one without the other, so nobody made you choose. AI rips the bundle apart. For the optimists, this is the best thing to happen to learning in a century. A tireless tutor for every student, instant feedback, personalized pacing, the death of the dead-eyed lecture hall. Used well, AI could finally force institutions to deliver on the teaching mission they've spent centuries claiming as their reason to exist. For the skeptics, the machine has been let loose & it isn't coming back under control. Call it Skynet for higher ed: once a model teaches the material better than the median professor, & a student can prove mastery without four years & six figures of debt, the institution can't put the thing back in the box. The emperor has no clothes. Strip away the instruction nobody needed the building for anyway, & you're left with what the university was actually charging for: the stamp, the gate, the brand. The degree stops mattering, & everyone finally admits it never really did. Two people who built their careers inside the machine. Two very different verdicts on whether it survives the decade. John Katzman founded The Princeton Review & now runs Noodle, building the infrastructure behind online degree programs. He has spent decades on the business of how education actually gets delivered & paid for. If you want the case that AI makes institutions more effective, not less, he's your guy. Akil Bello got his start in test prep under John Katzman at The Princeton Review. He went on to found Bell Curves & has spent thirty years studying how the educational industry actually works, who it serves, & what it obscures. He agrees AI will transform higher ed. He's less convinced institutions will lead that transformation rather than be dragged through it. UNMUTED is a discussion forum for the politically curious. Engaging. Accessible. Social. Open-minded is the name of the game. Join your people.

gary_2026_09_11_the_ai_briefing_by_start.title: The AI Briefing By Startup Grind - The Workforce Gap In AI Readiness
gary_2026_09_11_the_ai_briefing_by_start.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_09_11_the_ai_briefing_by_start.summary: Gary's Guide: The AI Briefing is a high-velocity roundtable for decision-makers brought to you by Startup Grind. We bypass the hype by dissecting one high-signal industry deck with a room of vetted founders, operators, & enterprise executives. No lectures-just a 60-minute deep-dive into the tactics & data defining your next quarter. The AI Briefing is a recurring AI deep-dive for decision-makers. Each month, we select one high-signal industry report, circulate it in advance, & meet to cut through the noise. This Month's Source: 2026 People Readiness Report (Kyndryl - Jun 2026) Kyndryl's newest survey of 1,100 business & technology leaders found something specific: workforce readiness dropped 6 points this year, to just 23%, even as broad AI deployment climbed to 57%. The gap between rollout speed & people readiness is widening. Leaders agree the technology itself isn't the constraint anymore. 79% say AI will outpace their organization's ability to adapt its workforce, governance, & operating model. And the confidence gap tracks straight down the org chart: half of executive leadership believes their teams are enthusiastic about AI, but only 3 in 10 individual contributors & entry-level employees agree. The same survey found 66% of organizations have already given AI agents unsupervised read & write access to their core systems of record. Trust & governance haven't caught up with what's already running in production. The Mission: Where adoption, the C-suite divide, & agentic governance actually meet Every AI Briefing this year has examined one piece of this from the top: how fast enterprises adopted, where leadership's confidence outran execution, & how governance is lagging behind autonomous agents. This session looks at the piece none of those touched directly: whether the workforce itself is ready, & what the data says happens to trust & outcomes when it isn't. We'll use Kyndryl's own segmentation, the small group of organizations it calls Pacesetters, to ground the conversation in what readiness actually requires versus what most organizations are doing instead. The Format: We'll open with the readiness numbers: adoption at 57%, workforce readiness at 23% & falling, & the widening distance between what executives report & what individual contributors experience. From there, the room works through Kyndryl's Pacesetter data: the 9% of organizations that redesigned roles, built change management, & got measurably better outcomes for it. What's replicable here, & what's easy to claim but hard to actually execute. gary_2026_09_15_tech_x_market_decoders.summary: Gary's Guide: We decode tech & market signals together - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Guests are invited to enjoy light refreshments while celebrating the diversity and innovation of contemporary printmaking. jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.title: RENT: The Musical
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.label: Music / Movies
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.place: ART HOUSE, 345 MARIN BLVD, JERSEY CITY
jc_culture_10004827_2026_09_24_rent_the_.summary: Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.
